title: Marketplace vertical integration acceptance heuristics and listing checklist
content:
Overview:

This working doc captures a compact set of heuristics and a pragmatic listing checklist specifically tailored for vertical integrations (ISV connectors, regulatory/industry bundles, and embedded partner flows) on cloud marketplaces. Goal: accelerate safe listings that reduce launch friction, limit back-and-forth with partners, and surface clear acceptance criteria for the Marketplace intake team.

Scope and audience:
- Intended for GTM owners, partner product managers, partner engineers, and listing intake reviewers.
- Focused on vertical integrations (healthcare, finance, legal, retail) and packaged connectors that carry additional compliance, data residency, or UI integration concerns.

Why a vertical-specific approach?
- Vertical integrations often have extra gating (HIPAA/PHI, PCI, local data residency).
- UX friction is higher: partners surface embedded flows, OAuth plumbing, and trial UX that can break marketplace provisioning.
- Acceptance speed matters: reducing ambiguous asks cuts review time by days.

High-level acceptance heuristics (fast checks to decide next step):
1) Safety & compliance posture (Quick pass/fail):
   - Does the partner claim any regulated-data handling (PHI, PCI, PII by EU/UK definitions)? If yes -> kick to Security & Compliance track.
   - Are there required certifications listed (SOC2, ISO27001, HIPAA)? If claimed, partner must provide artifact links or target timeline.
2) Entitlement parity and trial experience:
   - Does the listing and the console trial entitlement match the partner trial flow (30-day, usage-limited, or token-based)? Mismatch -> request reconciliation.
3) Integration UX friction:
   - Can a customer onboard within 10 minutes following listing flows? If expected onboarding > 1 hour, flag as 'high-friction' and request a streamlined quickstart page.
4) Billing & SKU mapping:
   - Is the partner mapping to a single SKU or tiered SKUs? Complex multi-SKU billing requires Marketplace Commerce review.
5) Telemetry & monitoring readiness:
   - Partner must provide at least two telemetry events we can surface (provisioned, first-request, error-rate). No telemetry -> recommend instrumentation before listing.

Core listing checklist (artifacts required before intake approval):
- Listing copy: 1-paragraph short description (<= 280 chars) and 300–500 char detailed summary. Provide 3 headline variants for A/B testing.
- Tile assets: square logo 512px, 128px, and 48px; 3 hero screenshots (1200x675) showing the product in customer context.
- One-pager PDF with architecture diagram (network boundaries, data flows) for security reviewers.
- Compliance artifacts: SOC2 or equivalent, privacy policy URL, data processing addendum (if applicable).
- Trial flow document: step-by-step onboarding guide including any required partner console steps, required API keys, and mock credentials for verification.
- Billing mapping: SKU names, unit metrics (tokens/month, seats, monthly active endpoints), trial entitlements and conversion triggers.
- Support SLA and escalation: email/portal link and expected response time during trial and post-sales.
- Contact list: partner PM, integration engineer, legal contact.

Copy & messaging guidance (playbook snippets):
- Short headline formula: outcome + audience + constraint (e.g., "Secure, low-latency LLM inference for fintech APIs").
- 280-char elevator: one-sentence value prop, one concrete metric (latency/cost/accuracy), one CTA (Start free trial / Request demo).
- Long description outline: problem statement -> how it works (1–2 bullets) -> benefits (3 bullets with metrics) -> compliance note -> CTA.

UX friction mitigation checklist (practical items to reduce rejections):
- Provide a pre-filled quickstart template that automates API key exchange (or a demo mode that bypasses production keys).
- Offer a sandbox dataset that mimics customer data but is scrubbed of PII; include it in screenshots.
- Host a 2-minute screencast demonstrating onboarding (link in listing assets).
- Ensure all OAuth redirect URIs and docs are listed in the one-pager.

Security & compliance gating (minimum required evidence):
- If handling regulated data: signed DPA or contract addendum and architecture diagram.
- If partner hosts on-prem or hybrid: clear network requirements, port lists, and KMS/HSM notes.
- Vulnerability management cadence (monthly scans or CVE monitoring) and a point of contact for incident response.

Telemetry and post-launch validation (small experiments to run after publish):
- Smoke test: one provisioning event, one first-request, one failure path per region.
- 7-day telemetry dashboard: activate simple KPIs (provision success rate, median onboarding time, first-24h usage).
- Collect customer-reported friction points via a 1-question post-onboard survey (Was onboarding straightforward? yes/no + optional comment).

Acceptance decision matrix (recommended reviewer outcomes):
- Approve: All required artifacts present, no regulated-data claims OR compliance artifacts provided, onboarding <= 10 minutes, billing mapping consistent.
- Conditional approve: Missing non-critical assets (additional screenshots, expanded copy) OR minor billing clarifications; publish to private beta with partner ops tag.
- Reject / Security hold: Regulated-data claim without DPA/compliance artifacts, or onboarding requires manual work > 1 hour.

Sample quick-copy variants (to include in the listing payload):
- Variant A (enterprise): "Redwood-native inference for healthcare apps — HIPAA-aware, private deployment options, and predictable per-request pricing. Start a secure trial."
- Variant B (developer-first): "Build fast with pre-configured model endpoints, auto-batching, and cost controls — launch an app-ready LLM in minutes. Try the 14-day sandbox."
- Variant C (vertical-focus): "Retail product discovery that reduces search latencies by 40% using cached embeddings and optimized quantized models. Request a partner demo."

Common rejection notes & suggested partner fix templates (short snippets reviewers can paste):
- Missing DPA: "Please provide an executed DPA or confirm in writing the timeline to execute — we cannot list partner handling PHI without a DPA."
- Onboarding confusion: "Please add a one-click sandbox or a 2-minute video walkthrough linked in the tile assets so customers can validate the flow quickly."
- Billing mismatch: "Clarify SKU unit metrics and confirm if trial usage will be billed post-conversion. If free during trial, indicate conversion conditions."

Operational playbook (next steps once partner is approved):
1) Tag listing as 'private beta' for 2 weeks while we monitor telemetry.
2) GTM: schedule co-marketing asset share; ask partner for 1 case study draft 30 days post-launch.
3) Product/Support: set an internal triage channel (Slack / ops playbook) for the first 72 hours after public listing.

Open questions and follow-ups (items to resolve before finalizing template):
- Do we require a minimum partner uptime SLA for marketplace tile publication? Proposal: 99.5% for enterprise verticals.
- Should we enforce a sandbox/demo requirement for all vertical listings? Proposal: Required for regulated verticals, optional otherwise.

Owners + next checkpoints:
- GTM owner: Aisha Patel (owns acceptance decision, copy variants, co-marketing plan).
- Partner engineering reviewer: Diego Ramirez (integration validation, telemetry).
- Security liaison: Maya Chen (compliance artifacts, DPA verification).
- Next checkpoint: intake runbook pilot with 3 partners scheduled for 2026-03-20; collect feedback and iterate.

References & artifacts: 
- Intake form template: CONFLUENCE-9821
- Example architecture diagram (anonymized): github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-assets/examples/arch-diagram.png
- Intake backlog: JIRA-PP-441

Notes to self (working ideas):
- Consider adding a tiny 'launch risk' score (0–10) computed from regulated-data flag, onboarding time, and billing complexity to standardize reviewer decisions.
- We should pre-populate copy snippets using partner-provided metrics to reduce iteration.

This file is a working draft — expect multiple iterations as we pilot with partners across fintech, retail, and healthcare.
